objective.statement: Read and write duplets in compound time and compare them with triplets in simple time.
successCriteria: I know a duplet puts two equal notes in the time of three.
I can say how long a duplet lasts.
I can write the same sound with two dotted notes instead.

explanation.text: In compound time every beat divides into three equal notes. A duplet changes that for one beat: it is a group of two equal notes played in the time normally taken by three. It is shown by a figure 2 above or below the notes.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 6/8: a duplet of two quavers, then a dotted crotchet.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: a duplet of quaver, quaver, dotted crotchet.

explanation.caption: 6/8: the duplet fills the first beat; the dotted crotchet fills the second.

explanation.text: A duplet of two quavers lasts as long as a dotted crotchet: three quavers' worth of time. Another way to write exactly the same sound is to put a dot after each of the two notes: two dotted quavers. Each is one and a half quavers long, and together they last three.

music.textAlternative: The same bar of 6/8 written with two dotted quavers instead of a duplet.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: dotted quaver, dotted quaver, dotted crotchet.

explanation.caption: Two dotted quavers sound the same as a duplet of quavers.

explanation.text: A duplet is the mirror of the triplet you met in Grade 2. A triplet puts three notes where two would fit, in simple time; a duplet puts two notes where three would fit, in compound time. Duplets can also be of other values: in 6/4 a duplet of two crotchets fills a dotted-minim beat.
Duplet: 2 notes in the time of 3, in compound time. Triplet: 3 notes in the time of 2, in simple time. A duplet fills one beat.

music.textAlternative: A duplet of two quavers and a dotted crotchet.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: a duplet of quaver, quaver, dotted crotchet.

steps: Tap two even notes in the time of one dotted-crotchet beat: the duplet.
Now tap the dotted crotchet in the same time.
The duplet divides the beat into two instead of three.
demonstration.textAlternative: A duplet of two quavers fills one beat of 6/8, like a dotted crotchet.

guided.prompt: In 12/8, a duplet of two quavers fills one beat. Which single note lasts the same time as the whole duplet?

music.textAlternative: A duplet of two quavers marked 2.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: a duplet of quaver, quaver.

quaver.reason: The duplet is two notes, so it lasts longer than one quaver: it fills a whole beat.

dotted-quaver.reason: A dotted quaver is one and a half quavers. The duplet fills three quavers' worth of time: one whole beat.

crotchet.reason: Two quavers written normally would last quavers×2. The duplet squeezes them into the time of three.

hints: A duplet puts two notes where three would fit.
A duplet of two quavers is played in the time normally taken by three: one whole beat of 12/8.

feedback.correct: Yes: the duplet fills one whole beat.

mistakes.tuplet-total-wrong: A tuplet still fills a fixed amount of time. Check which beat it replaces.
mistakes.tuplet-number-wrong: Count the notes that share the beat — that's the number to write over the group.
mistakes.written-value-wrong: Use the note value the group would have if it divided normally — then add the tuplet number.
mistakes.simple-compound-confusion: Count the equal notes in a beat: two means simple time, three means compound time.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Ask: how many notes, in the time of how many?

provenance.notes: Original wording. Follows Grade 4 outcome 4 and First Steps Grade 4 section 4 (p. 82): a duplet is two equal notes in the time normally taken by three; the figure 2; the two-dotted-notes alternative. The book's comparison table (2/4 with triplets, 6/8 with duplets) is not reproduced; the triplet comparison here is verbal. Rhythms with duplets always fill exactly one beat per group.
